subject: Mathematics
textbook: Balbharati Mathematics & Statistics Part I and Part II (Arts & Science)
source_doc: LWS Maths XI Refactored Syllabus v4.docx
purpose: Spiral chapter plan (spine): the cognitively-sequenced teaching order. Deep-dive subtopic/concept/source mappings live in maths-xi-deep-dive.json, keyed by unit_no.
session_model: Based on 50-minute periods with ~30% time for in-class problem solving.
notes: Units are numbered 1-27 in teaching order; each unit's board chapter (or 'NDA-supplementary'/'SSC') is shown in the Board Source column.
18 board chapters + 6 numerical / NDA-supplementary units (Binary Numbers, Quadratic Equations, Linear Inequalities, Logarithms, Statistics I, Regression & Correlation) = 27 units.

Numerical foundation is front-loaded in Phase 1 (Binary Numbers, Quadratic Equations, Logarithms, Statistics I) - real numerical content, not a decontextualized primer; pair with a standing daily calculation drill.
Statistics is a spiral: Statistics I (central tendency) in Phase 1 -> Measures of Dispersion (Statistics II) in Phase 6 -> Regression & Correlation in Phase 6.
Phase 6 'flexible' applies to Measures of Dispersion; Probability has a hard floor after Phase 3 (needs P&C + Sets).

guiding_principles.meaning: Trig split into 3 parts (Phase 2, Phase 4 calculus bridge, Phase 5). Complex Numbers split into 2 parts (Phase 3 algebra, Phase 5 geometry). Students return to each concept at greater depth.
Sets, Relations, Functions moved to Phase 1. The board places them at Chapter 5-6 of Part II, taught after half the syllabus without formally defining a function.
Board places all three conics in one chapter. Parabola and Ellipse/Hyperbola taught separately; each is its own vocabulary, standard-form family, and problem universe.
Limits and Continuity kept as separate units despite being one board chapter. Trig Part C placed before Limits because inverse-trig domain-restriction thinking primes limit intuition.

Central tendency (Statistics I) is front-loaded to Phase 1 - it is pure calculation (numerical foundation) and the prerequisite for every dispersion measure. Measures of Dispersion (Statistics II), Regression & Correlation, and Probability sit in Phase 6 as flexible / computation-based blocks.

50-minute periods, ~30% in-class problem solving. The ~145 sessions cover the original board chapters; the 6 numerical / NDA-supplementary units added (Binary Numbers, Quadratic Equations, Linear Inequalities, Logarithms, Statistics I, Regression) have sessions TBD.

phases.name: Mathematical Language & Foundation
phases.blurb: Build the vocabulary. Every chapter here is a tool that every later chapter will depend on.

phases.name: Trigonometry (Three-Part Spiral)
phases.blurb: The largest conceptual arc. Basics now, identities after algebra, equations last.

phases.name: Core Algebra
phases.blurb: The algebra engine, built on Phase 1 language and Phase 2 trig fluency.

phases.name: Geometry
phases.blurb: Two-dimensional geometry built on the algebraic tools now available.

phases.name: Calculus Foundation
phases.blurb: A complete mindset shift: thinking about 'approach' and 'behaviour' rather than exact values.

phases.name: Statistics and Probability
phases.blurb: Computation-based relief chapters. Flexible placement within the year.

units.title: Sets and Relations
units.why_here: Defines the language of all mathematics (function, domain, membership); teaching it first makes everything downstream cleaner and faster.

units.title: Binary Numbers
units.why_here: [NDA-supplementary] Number-system topic NDA tests (binary arithmetic, conversion; 13 PYQs) with no board chapter; self-contained, placed early in the foundation phase.

units.title: Quadratic Equations
units.why_here: [NDA-supplementary] Quadratics are Class-10/SSC content NDA tests as a distinct chapter (Vieta's, nature of roots; 63 PYQs); revised early and feeds Complex Numbers A.

units.title: Functions — Concept and Algebra
units.why_here: The single most important concept in school maths; placed right after Sets so every later chapter uses the language properly.

units.title: Linear Inequalities
units.board_source: NDA-supplementary - NCERT-11 Ch5; board folds into XII LP
units.why_here: [NDA-supplementary] Solving/graphing linear inequalities; part of the Functions block (domain determination). NCERT-11 has it (Ch5); the Maharashtra board folds it into XII Linear Programming.

units.title: Functions — Exponential and Logarithmic
units.why_here: Log is best understood as a function; log laws are prerequisites for log-function domains and reappear in Differentiation and Limits.

units.title: Logarithms
units.board_source: NDA depth - board embeds in XI Functions §6.1.5
units.why_here: [NDA-supplementary] NDA has a standalone Logarithms chapter (identities, change of base, log equations; 27 PYQs); the board embeds log in Functions (U2B). Placed right after 2B to deepen to NDA level.

units.title: Measures of Central Tendency (Statistics I)
units.board_source: SSC (Class 10) central tendency; board embeds combined mean in Measures of Dispersion
units.why_here: [Numerical foundation] Mean, median, mode + frequency distributions - pure calculation, SSC-rooted, and the prerequisite for every dispersion measure (variance/SD/CV need the mean). Front-loaded to build numerical fluency early and to precede Measures of Dispersion (Statistics II) in Phase 6. NDA's #2 subtopic (75 PYQ).

units.title: Trigonometry Part A — Angle Measurement & Ratios
units.why_here: Rebuilds the SSC right-triangle view into a radian/unit-circle/all-six-ratios foundation; identities and equations cannot start until this is solid.

units.title: Trigonometry Part B — Identities
units.why_here: Placed after algebraic fluency; the deliberate gap since Part A makes identities feel like new tools rather than the same overwhelming chapter.

units.title: Complex Numbers Part A — Algebra
units.why_here: Purely algebraic (define i, a+bi arithmetic, modulus, conjugate); the geometric interpretation is held for Phase 5 after trig fluency.

units.title: Sequences and Series
units.why_here: Natural progression from algebraic comfort; internal order matters AP -> GP -> HP -> Special Series.

units.title: Permutations and Combinations
units.why_here: Counting follows from set theory; strict internal chain counting-principle -> factorial -> permutation -> combination.

units.title: Methods of Induction and Binomial Theorem
units.why_here: Induction is the proof tool and binomial its prime application; binomial coefficients are nCr, so it follows P&C.

units.title: Determinants and Matrices
units.why_here: Determinants and matrix inverse are interdependent; order matrix arithmetic -> determinants -> inverse/systems; placed after strong algebra.

units.title: Straight Line
units.why_here: Students now have systems of equations (Matrices) to handle angle bisectors, concurrency, and family of lines properly rather than mechanically.

units.title: Circle
units.why_here: Follows straight lines (tangents need perpendicularity; 3-point circle needs simultaneous equations); conceptual bridge to conics.

units.title: Conic Sections Part A — Parabola
units.why_here: Conics split by type; parabola first as the simplest (one axis of symmetry, one focus).

units.title: Conic Sections Part B — Ellipse and Hyperbola
units.board_source: Part I, Ch. 7 (ellipse and hyperbola portions)
units.why_here: Taught together as structural mirrors (only the sign differs); kept after parabola so the eccentricity framework (e<1 vs e>1) makes sense.

units.title: Trigonometry Part C — Equations and Inverse Functions
units.board_source: Part I, Ch. 2 + Ch. 3 (equation and inverse portions)
units.why_here: Inverse-trig domain-restriction primes limit thinking; needs identity fluency (Part B) and periodicity (Part A); eases into the calculus section.

units.title: Complex Numbers Part B — Geometry and Applications
units.why_here: Argand plane / polar form / De Moivre need full trig fluency (Parts A, B, C done); students now genuinely understand r(cos t + i sin t).

units.title: Limits
units.why_here: The biggest conceptual jump ('approaching' vs 'equalling'); separated from Continuity, which the board combines.

units.title: Continuity
units.why_here: Deliberately separate from Limits; a standalone chapter forces students to articulate limit-exists vs value-equals.

units.title: Differentiation
units.why_here: Most content-heavy chapter; four sequential stages, first principles not skipped; geometric interpretation links back to Straight Lines.

units.title: Measures of Dispersion (Statistics II)
units.why_here: Measuring spread: range, quartile & mean deviation, variance, standard deviation, coefficient of variation. Builds on the mean from Statistics I; the second stage of the statistics spiral. Flexible/computation-based placement.

units.title: Regression & Correlation
units.why_here: [NDA-supplementary] NDA Statistics includes regression & correlation (27 PYQs); absent from Maharashtra Measures of Dispersion. Placed after Dispersion (needs mean/SD).

units.title: Probability
units.why_here: Placed last because good problems need P&C fluency (Phase 3) and set-theory language (Phase 1).
